rulers.name: Filipe de Brito e Nicote
rulers.note: Governor from 1599 for Arakan; declared independence in 1603; recognised by Goa and the Portuguese court; impaled in 1613.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; the First Toungoo Empire row has no shape here 1600-1613 and kingdom-of-mrauk-u's shapes do not reach it). Thanlyin page: 'in 1603, De Brito declared independence ... successfully established Portuguese rule over Syriam'. The pages give no extent beyond the city; the 40 km circle follows the kingdom-of-mrauk-u dossier's 1599 occupation (first-toungoo-empire uses 60 km for its 1613 gain, calling it 'Syriam and the Pegu country', which these pages do not support). No area.

ledger.note: 1603: de Brito declares Syriam independent of Arakan. 'In 1603, De Brito declared independence, and after defeating the invading Arakanese navy in 1604 and 1605, successfully established Portuguese rule over Syriam (or Sirião in Portuguese) under the Portuguese viceroy of Goa.' He had become governor in 1599 'commanding three frigates and 3,000 men'.

region.text: Syriam (Thanlyin) and its district at the mouth of the Pegu river; the pages describe only 'the city'

ledger.note: 1604: the Arakanese fleet attacks Syriam. De Brito defeated 'the invading Arakanese navy in 1604 and 1605'; in the 1605 Syriam battles he captured crown prince Min Khamaung.

region.text: Syriam (Thanlyin) and its district at the mouth of the Pegu river; the pages describe only 'the city'

ledger.note: 1605: the Arakanese attacks fail. The 1605 Syriam battles end with de Brito capturing Prince Min Khamaung; Toungoo's Natshinnaung also came to Syriam (undated).

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by se-01-f and se-01-g as 'Portuguese Syriam (Filipe de Brito)'. Two pages opened. It lasted ten years, the minimum the brief gives, and covers one city: the dossier is deliberately small. Not settled: (1) the extent: both pages name only the city, so the first-toungoo-empire 1613 gain 'Syriam and the Pegu country' (60 km) is wider than anything here; (2) the pages disagree with kingdom-of-mrauk-u's March 1603 and the 1599 dates only by silence; (3) the vassal status (a Portuguese 'kingdom' under the viceroy of Goa; subject of Ayutthaya after de Brito married Bannya Dala's daughter, undated); (4) the Dhammazedi Bell was removed from the Shwedagon in 1608; (5) wikipedia is null because no page of its own exists in the pages opened (the topic sits in the de Brito and Thanlyin articles); family is 'portugal' as the one Portuguese-ruled state of the region.
